To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complex collinear spin partial wave decomposition of generalized parton distribution and generalized distribution amplings provides the basis for a versatile and flexible parametrization of these quantities, that the Mellin moments can be approximated by Regge trajectories in the t -channel, and that the partial wave decomposition is essential to calculate next-to-next-to leading order effects in deeply virtual Compton Scattering.
the conformal spin partial-wave expansion of generalized partons and distribution amplitutes is a powerful tool to analyze the non-perturbatic structure of hadrons.

the complex collinear spin partial wave expansion provides an elegant parameterization for generalized parton distributions, that this representation allows for a rather simple numerical treatment, that the conformal moments are related to the Mellin moments and that this representation allows to perform the evolution to next-to-leading order in a simple way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the non-perturbatic properties of QCD.
a new representation of non-perturbatively calculable functions that are relevant for the analysis of the deeply virtual Compton process.
the development and analysis of new methods for the study of non-perturbatively defined functions, such as generalized parton distributions, generalized distribution amplitutes, and their moments.

the conformal representation of GPDs and GAs is a very powerful tool for a systematic and comprehensive study of the non-perturbatively unknown quantities.
this representation is a powerful tool for the phenomenology and analysis of deeply virtual processes.
the conformal partial wave expansion of GPDs and GDAs is a very powerful and flexible tool for the phenomenological and theoretical description of hard exclusive reactions.

we are now able to calculate the full next-to-leading order evolution for all GPDs and all twist-2 GDA’s.

conformal symmetry is a very powerful tool to study non-perturbatively the structure of hadrons and their interactions.
